en.title: Minimum Number of Permutation Operations
en.description:
Given a permutation p of 1..n. One operation simultaneously sets temp[i]=arr[p[i]] for every 1-based index i, and then sets arr=temp. For an initial array of any n distinct elements, find the minimum number of operations needed to return to the initial array, modulo 1,000,000,007.

This site adds the standard input/output protocol; it does not imply that the original site's function-style problem had this protocol.
en.input: n; the second line contains the n permutation values p[i].
en.output: Output the minimum number of operations modulo 1,000,000,007.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof, and complexity.
hints: Decompose the permutation into cycles; the number of operations needed to restore the original array is the least common multiple of all cycle lengths.
